newsitem.title: USA: Letters went to Clinton, Gore about Cosby.
newsitem.headline: Letters went to Clinton, Gore about Cosby.

text.p: The woman claiming to be Bill Cosby's illegitimate daughter and an alleged accomplice sent a letter to President Bill Clinton to put pressure on the entertainer to pay her, a witness testified on Wednesday.
Copies of the letters also were sent to dozens of influential officials and were read by the jury.
Autumn Jackson, 22, is accused of threatening to expose Cosby as her father in an attempt to extort $40 million from the actor.

She and her co-defendants Jose Medina, 51, and Boris Sabas, 42, are charged with conspiracy, extortion and engaging in interstate commerce to commit crimes. If convicted, they face prison terms of 12 years and fines of $750,000.

Although Cosby wasn't named, he was clearly identified as a deadbeat father in the Jan. 10 letter, according to testimony from Placido Macaraeg, a publicist for a proposed children's television show called "Down on the Farm" that Jackson, Medina and Sabas were trying to launch.

Macaraeg testified that he was present in a hotel room with the three defendants when Jackson called Cosby's lawyer demanding $40 million to keep her from telling the press about her claim to be Cosby's daughter.

Macaraeg said Medina was telling Jackson what to say to the lawyer "and was writing words on a piece of paper and handing it to her." He said Jackson was frustrated when she got off the phone with the lawyer because she said he didn't understand the term "settlement."
"If he doesn't want this story to get out, he's going to have to pay a lot of money," Macaraeg quotes Medina as saying.
Cosby testified on Tuesday that he had sex once with Jackson's mother but denies being her father. Actual paternity is not an issue in the trial.
Among the other officials who were sent the letter were Vice-President Al Gore, Rev. Jesse Jackson, California Gov. Pete Wilson, and the mayors of Los Angeles, New York and Washington, D.C.
Macaraeg testified that the three-page letter was signed by Medina but that Jackson contributed to its contents. He read out parts of the letter in court.

"Deadbeat Father ... Autumn is left in the cold, penniless and homeless. Autumn, the daughter of a CBS mega-star on many of the most watched CBS prime time television shows..." writes Medina, adding that Jackson was now on his production staff.
The letter also alleged that Jackson's "deadbeat father and mother took harsh parenting actions against her."

Macaraeg also testified that on Jan. 17, he heard a taped conversation between Medina and Jackson's mother Shawn Thompson in which Thompson said her daughter "should stop what she was doing because it was extortion and could get the people around her hurt."
